title: Why chemo can cause hair loss
body: Your body makes new cells by dividing. One cell splits into two.
Chemo works on cells while they divide. Cancer cells divide much more often than most normal cells, so chemo can damage and destroy them.
Some healthy cells divide fast too. The cells that make hair grow are one example. So are the cells lining the mouth and gut, and the blood-making cells in bone marrow.
Chemo can't tell a busy cancer cell from a busy hair cell. That's why some types of chemo make hair fall out.
Healthy cells can replace or repair themselves, so this damage doesn't usually last. Most hair loss from chemo is reversible once treatment is over.
realWorld: Hair often grows back 2 to 3 months after chemo ends.
